# SPE Round 3 Plan

Round 3 tests one fix. Config C gets its outage status check back as its own tool. Round 2 showed that the naive guess was closer than my prediction in 4 of 5 rows. So this round starts from round 2's measured numbers. I move a number only when a failure ID gives me a reason.

This round runs autonomously. I record each choice as a logged default in `spe/spec/disagreements.md`. The user owns each one and can reverse it.

## 1. Specify

### Decisions on the round 2 proposals

| ID | Decision | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | Adopt | F4 shows that C never called the status check inside the merged tool. Splitting it back out tests that cause directly. The new config is called C-split. It differs from r02 C in this one change only. |
| P2 | Adopt, with a changed reason | The "near ceiling" reason is weak. An accuracy of 0.86 still leaves 14% of tickets wrong. I adopt P2 because mixed billing and outage tickets are the exact case where F4 hurts. The 10 new tickets go in a separate "hard set". The original tickets stay the "old set" so that round 3 numbers stay comparable with round 2. |
| P3 | Adopt as a logged default | In r02, D was the worst config on accuracy (0.74), and its cost rose. Dropping D frees budget for P4. F6 stays open and is marked "parked, D dropped in r03". The alternative would keep D and add a retry cap to test F6. That alternative is logged in disagreements.md for the user. |
| P4 | Adopt | B missed by 0.02 at 3 trials per cell. Five trials per cell reduce trial noise. This change does not move any expected value. It only narrows the spread. |

### Round 3 requirement table (appended to `spe/spec/spec.md`)

| ID | Requirement | Source | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| R3-1 | C-split exposes the outage status check as its own tool. All other C tools stay merged as in r02. | r02 F4, P1 | The C-split config file lists `status_check` as a separate tool. A diff against r02 C shows only that change. |
| R3-2 | The ticket set adds 10 mixed billing and outage tickets. Each ticket has `label.category`, `label.priority`, and a written note that applies the primary-category rule (see default D2). | P2 | A schema check on the answer key passes. The grader oracle scores 1.0 on all 10 tickets. |
| R3-3 | Results are reported for the old set, the hard set, and both sets combined. Old set numbers are the ones compared with r02. | Decision: comparability with r02 | The results JSON has all three blocks for every metric. |
| R3-4 | The configs are A, B, and C-split. D does not run. | P3, r02 F6 | The Workflow config list has exactly 3 entries. |
| R3-5 | Each config and ticket cell runs 5 trials. Split cells get extra trials up to a cap. | P4 | Trial counts in the results JSON match. |
| R3-6 | The grader reads priority only from `label.priority`. | r02 F5 | A selftest case has a draft reply that says P1 and a label that says P3. The grader must score it as P3. |
| R3-7 | The verdict rule is fixed before the run (see section 2). | Decision: B's r02 miss was inside noise | The rule is written in `r03.yaml` before launch. |
| R3-8 | A new metric records the status-check call rate on outage tickets. Code computes it from each trial's `tool_calls`. | r02 F4 | `grade.py status_check_called` exists and passes the selftest. |
| R3-9 | Trials cannot read graders, answer keys, predictions, the spec, the prediction log, or the failures file. | SPE method | Trials run in a temp directory that holds only the ticket and the tool stubs. A transcript scan voids any trial that touched a protected path. |
| R3-10 | Model spend has a hard cap of $15. Any trial that would cross the cap is skipped and logged. | SPE method | A skip log exists. The total spend in the results is at or under $15. |

### Logged defaults (added to `spe/spec/disagreements.md`, owner: the user)

- **D1. Drop D.** This is the default. The alternative is "D plus a retry cap" to test F6.
- **D2. Primary-category rule for mixed tickets.** If the service is down at the time of the ticket, the category is outage. Otherwise it is billing. I write the 10 tickets and their labels. A separate Opus agent labels them blind before the run. Any ticket where the two labels disagree goes to the user as an open question, and that ticket is held out of scoring. The user should spot-check these labels, because I wrote both the tickets and the rule.
- **D3. Verdict tolerance.** An accuracy prediction is a hit when it is within 0.02 of the measured value. A cost prediction is a hit when it is within 20%. Under this rule, B's r02 result would count as a hit. I do not rewrite the r02 verdicts. The "Closer" column is still reported for every row.
- **D4. Unchanged rows are set by rule.** Some rows have no change. Those are priority accuracy and cost per ticket for A and B. Their predicted value is the r02 regraded measured value, copied into `r03.yaml` before launch. These rows do not appear in the round 2 summary I worked from. The copy is mechanical and involves no judgment.

## 2. Predict

"Same as last round" means r02 measured, after the F5 regrade. On the hard set there is no last round. So the naive guess there is the same config's r02 old-set number.

The grader checks are `grade.py category_exact`, `grade.py priority_exact` (which reads `label.priority`), `grade.py status_check_called`, and `cost.py per_ticket`, which uses token usage and the price table.

### Old set (compared with r02)

| Metric | Config | Same as last round | Predicted | Grader check | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| category accuracy | A | 0.86 | 0.86 | category_exact | A is unchanged. My r02 prediction for A was a hit. |
| category accuracy | B | 0.86 | 0.86 | category_exact | B is unchanged. The rise I predicted for B in r02 did not happen, so I drop it. |
| category accuracy | C-split | 0.80 | 0.82 | category_exact | C fell 0.04 from r01 when the tools were merged. Some of that drop likely came from outage tickets that lost the status check. I do not know how much, so I move half way back. |
| priority accuracy | A | r02 value | r02 value | priority_exact | A is unchanged (D4). |
| priority accuracy | B | r02 value | r02 value | priority_exact | B is unchanged (D4). |
| priority accuracy | C-split | 0.71 | 0.76 | priority_exact | Because of F4, outage tickets got P3. The split tool lets C-split see outage status again. I stay below r01's 0.78 because r01 was graded before the F5 fix. |
| status-check call rate on outage tickets | A | none | 0.95 | status_check_called | A always had the separate tool. No r02 failure reports missed calls in A. |
| status-check call rate on outage tickets | B | none | 0.95 | status_check_called | Same reason as A. |
| status-check call rate on outage tickets | C-split | about 0 on T17 (F4) | 0.95 | status_check_called | C-split now sees the same tool that A sees. |
| cost per ticket | A | r02 value | r02 value | cost.py per_ticket | A is unchanged (D4). |
| cost per ticket | B | r02 value | r02 value | cost.py per_ticket | B is unchanged (D4). |
| cost per ticket | C-split | r02 C | r02 C x 1.05 | cost.py per_ticket | C-split adds one more tool schema to the context and one more call on outage tickets. |

### Hard set (new, no baseline, low confidence)

| Metric | Config | Naive (r02 old set) | Predicted | Grader check | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| category accuracy | A | 0.86 | 0.70 | category_exact | Mixed tickets have two plausible categories. I expect much more error than on the old set. |
| category accuracy | B | 0.86 | 0.70 | category_exact | Same reason as A. Nothing in B targets mixed tickets. |
| category accuracy | C-split | 0.80 | 0.66 | category_exact | I keep C-split's old-set gap of 0.04 below A. Its billing tools stay merged. |
| priority accuracy | A | r02 value | 0.75 | priority_exact | An outage should lead to P1 or P2. The billing text in the same ticket pulls some answers toward P3. |
| priority accuracy | B | r02 value | 0.75 | priority_exact | Same reason as A. |
| priority accuracy | C-split | 0.71 | 0.70 | priority_exact | The status check is restored. Merged billing tools still add billing weight on these tickets. |
| status-check call rate on outage tickets | A, B, C-split | none | 0.90 | status_check_called | Billing text may lead the agent to skip the outage check on some mixed tickets. |

Three old-set rows move away from "same as last round", and each one cites F4. Every hard-set row moves, because the hard set has no history. Hard-set rows are scored, but they do not count toward the 3-round match streak.

## 3. Evaluate

### Files

- `spe/evals/harness/r03-workflow.js` is the Workflow script. It holds `const ROUND = 3` and builds every round label (`r03`) from that constant. No prompt text has a round number written by hand.
- `spe/evals/tickets/hard-r03/` holds the 10 new tickets. The answer key goes in the existing answer key folder, which trials cannot reach.
- `spe/evals/configs/C-split.*` is a copy of r02 C with the status check split out.
- `spe/evals/results/r03.json` holds the results.

### Gates before launch (any failure halts the round and I report it)

1. **Preflight.** Confirm that pwd, the git remote, and the branch match this repo. The `spe/` tree must have no uncommitted changes.
2. **Label check (D2).** A blind Opus agent labels the 10 hard tickets. Any ticket where its label disagrees with mine is held out and logged.
3. **Grader selftest.** The oracle scores 1.0. An empty output scores 0. A wrong output scores 0. The F5 conflict case scores from `label.priority`. `status_check_called` returns true on a fixture that contains the call and false on a fixture that does not.
4. **Control.** Regrade the r02 transcripts with the current grader. The result must match the r02 regraded numbers exactly. This control also gives r02 status-check call rates as context. It does not change any saved prediction.
5. **Dry run.** Run 1 trial each in 3 cells: A on T17, C-split on T17, and C-split on hard ticket 01. Check the trial schema, the peek scan, and the cost per trial. Dry-run trials are not scored. If the measured cost per trial times the planned trial count is over $15, the round halts.

### Workflow steps

1. Run the main grid: configs A, B, and C-split, times all old-set and hard-set tickets, times 5 trials.
2. Each trial returns a schema: `ticket_id`, `config`, `trial`, `label.category`, `label.priority`, `draft_reply`, `tool_calls[]`, `tokens_in`, `tokens_out`, `cost_usd`, and `paths_read[]`.
3. Code checks run first. They cover schema validity, category match, priority match, status-check calls, and cost. No metric this round needs a judge.
4. The peek scan voids any trial that read a grader, answer key, prediction, spec, `prediction-log.md`, or `failures.md` path. Voids are logged with the trial ID.
5. A cell is split when its 5 trials divide 3 to 2 on category or priority correctness. A split cell gets up to 3 extra trials. Extra trials across the whole run are capped at 60.
6. The budget guard checks running spend before each trial. It skips any trial that would cross $15 and logs the skip.
7. A failure analysis agent (Opus) reads every wrong trial. It maps each one to F1 through F6, or it proposes a new failure starting at F7 with the trial IDs.
8. A completeness critic (Opus) checks four things. Every predicted cell has a measured value. Every void and skip is logged. Every hard-set hold-out is listed. Old-set, hard-set, and combined blocks all exist.

### Workflow arguments

```json
{
  "configs": ["A", "B", "C-split"],
  "ticket_sets": ["old", "hard-r03"],
  "trials_per_cell": 5,
  "extra_trials_per_split_cell": 3,
  "extra_trials_total_cap": 60,
  "budget_usd": 15,
  "concurrency": 6,
  "analysis_model": "opus",
  "trial_model": "from each config file"
}
```

### Cost estimate (unmeasured)

The old set has at least 17 tickets, because T17 exists. For this estimate I assume 40 tickets as an upper bound. That gives 3 configs x 50 tickets x 5 trials = 750 trials, plus up to 60 extra trials. At $0.004 to $0.01 per trial, the trials cost about $3 to $8. The label check, failure analysis, and critic add about $2. The hard cap is $15. The dry run replaces this estimate with a measured cost per trial before the main run starts.

### Halt and report

The round halts and I report when any of these happens:

- the budget cap is hit
- an answer key leaks to a trial
- a gate shows a broken grader
- a label dispute leaves fewer than 6 usable hard tickets
- a choice comes up that only the user can make

I do not push, deploy, or send anything.

## 4. Order of work and commits (local only, no push, no attribution lines)

1. Save the user's prompt verbatim to `spe/spec/transcripts/2026-10-21-r03.md`. Append the R3 table to `spec.md` and the D1 to D4 defaults to `disagreements.md`. Commit `SPE r03 specify: split outage check, add hard set, drop D, 5 trials`.
2. Copy this plan to `spe/plans/r03.md`. Write `spe/predictions/r03.yaml`. The file starts with `# Saved before the eval ran. Do not edit after the run.` It also holds the round, the date, the author ("Claude, approved by the user in plan mode", run autonomously at the user's request), the configs, every number, a Why for each number, `same_as_last_round`, and the D3 verdict rule. The D4 rows are filled from the r02 regraded values at this step. Commit `SPE r03 predict: C-split recovers priority to 0.76, A and B hold`.
3. Build the tickets, the C-split config, the grader additions, and the Workflow script. Run gates 1 to 5. Commit `SPE r03 evaluate (harness)`.
4. Launch the Workflow. It returns at launch. I wait for the completion notice.
5. Write `r03.json`. Commit `SPE r03 evaluate (results): <headline from measured numbers>`.

## 5. Close-out after the completion notice

- **`spe/prediction-log.md`.** Add a round 3 section with these columns: Metric, Config, Predicted, Measured, Same as last round, Verdict, Closer. Under "Which Why broke", quote each missed Why and name the wrong assumption. If the naive guess beat my predictions again, I say so plainly.
- **`spe/failures.md`.** Add each new failure type with its name, kind, round, What, How to spot it, Seen in, and Fix. Update F4 to fixed or still open based on the C-split call rate. Mark F6 as parked. A grader bug found after the run counts as a failure. Original and regraded numbers go side by side.
- **Next round.** Add a "Proposed for round 4" table to `spec.md`, and write `spe/predictions/r04-draft.yaml` with `status: draft`.
- **Wrap-up.** Update `spe/README.md`. Commit `SPE r03 learn: <one line>` and tag `spe-r03`.
- **Stop check.** The match streak is at most 1 after r02, so the loop continues. If every config passes everything on both sets, round 4 needs harder tickets or stricter graders.
